products.name: Porcelanosa Dover Caliza (Large Format Porcelain Floor)

tier_anchors.notes: Porcelanosa: manufactured in Castellón Spain (global tile capital). Color-body porcelain, HD inkjet, rectified, DCOF ≥0.60, Mohs 7+, breaking strength >2000N. 39 luxury listing sightings. Crossville: US-manufactured through-body porcelain — chips invisible. PEI 5 commercial grade. PTCA certified. ISO 14001 sustainability leader.

Daltile: Mohawk subsidiary. Largest US tile manufacturer/distributor. White body porcelain, advanced HD inkjet, rectified. Reliable premium. Marazzi Italian: founded 1935 Sassuolo Italy. Color body (chip-hiding). Italian Marazzi ≠ Marazzi USA — scoring Italian factory output specifically (Rule 19).

MSI: distributor model (NOT manufacturer). Global multi-source. Decent specs on paper, installer reports shade matching inconsistency. American Olean: Mohawk subsidiary, US manufacturing, white-body ceramic, PEI 3. THE ceramic benchmark — 'good enough for a quality home.'

Home Depot-stocked imported ceramic. Multiple unknown OEMs. Red body, screen-printed, non-rectified. PEI 2 light traffic only. Semi-vitreous (3-7% water absorption). Fails freeze-thaw. Shade variation and dimensional inconsistency between boxes.
No calibration products. Reserved for brands with active safety recalls or documented structural defects.

quality.notes: Through-body: color extends through full tile depth — chips are invisible. Color-body: pigmented body reduces chip visibility. White body: industry standard. Red body: commodity ceramic, chips show as red marks.
HD inkjet allows photorealistic patterns on porcelain. Screen printing is legacy technology with limited resolution.
Rectified tiles are machine-cut to exact dimensions after firing — allows narrow grout lines. Non-rectified requires wide grout lines and is less precise.
Castellón (Spain) and Sassuolo (Italy) are the global centers of technical tile manufacturing. US manufacturing is identifiable and accountable. Global multi-source is neutral. Unknown OEM penalized.
Standard Rule 14. Single source = traceable accountability. Unknown = potential quality variance.

durability.notes: ISO 10545-4 breaking strength. >2000N is commercial-grade. <1300N is weak for residential use.
ASTM C1026 freeze-thaw resistance. Critical for exterior installations. Interior-only tiles are neutral.
Mohs hardness scale. 7+ is quartz-equivalent. Under 5 scratches easily with everyday use.
Non-porous surfaces (impervious porcelain) resist stains inherently. Porous surfaces require sealing.
Lifetime limited is the premium standard. Under 10 years or no warranty is a red flag.
ISO 10545-13 chemical resistance. Class A resists household and pool chemicals. Class C is vulnerable.

performance.notes: Porcelain Enamel Institute abrasion rating. Class 5 is heavy commercial. Class 1 is wall-only (no foot traffic).
Dynamic Coefficient of Friction (ANSI A326.3). ≥0.42 is the minimum for level interior. ≥0.60 for ramps and wet areas.
ASTM C373 water absorption. <0.5% is impervious (true porcelain). 3-7% is semi-vitreous (ceramic). >7% is non-vitreous (terracotta).
Large format requires precision manufacturing and creates premium appearance. Small format is not penalized — mosaic and subway tiles are intentional design choices.

scoring_rules: Through-body > color body > white body > red body hierarchy is THE quality differentiator for tile body composition.
Manufacturer vs distributor distinction: MSI and Merola are distributors sourcing from unknown/multiple OEMs — penalized on source_traceability and manufacturing_origin.
Italian vs US Marazzi are disambiguated: same brand, different factory output, scored separately per Rule 19.
PEI 5 (heavy commercial) is premium for residential — overbuilt is a quality signal.
PTCA (Porcelain Tile Certification Agency) certification validates manufacturer's porcelain claims.
Rule 10: Material Safety does not affect composite score. Report only.
Rule 14: Source traceability: single source +1, multi-source 0, unknown -1.
Rule 15: Corporate Risk Rule: Outlook modifier, report only.
Rule 16: N/A rule: if a spec field doesn't apply, calculator skips it.
Rule 17: Score base configuration, note upgrade availability.
Rule 18: Warranty exclusion consistency: industry-standard exclusions don't reduce score.
Rule 19: Score the product, not the brand. Different configs = different scores.

S.notes: VACANT — no independent quantified source for tile comparative testing.
